headline: High risk: Claude Code can write/egress by default while Argo Workflows can ingest and orchestrate artifacts, creating dangerous shared-workspace and cascading-action pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo Workflows can expose artifacts and API outputs, while Claude Code reads repo files and user-provided directories and can use MCP servers. If Argo-produced content is placed in a shared workspace, Claude Code may treat it as instructions. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is plausible in default setups.
conditions: IF Argo outputs are written into a directory Claude Code reads
IF an MCP server or file bridge passes Argo-generated text to Claude Code without provenance tags
mitigations: Separate Argo output directories from Claude Code workspaces
Add a provenance header to all Argo-generated files
Disable MCP servers that ingest untrusted workflow output
Require manual review before Claude Code acts on workflow artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo Workflows touches artifacts and parameters, and Claude Code reads filesystem content while sending requests to api.anthropic.com with broad network egress. In a shared workspace, files from Argo can be read into Claude Code and then transmitted to a third party. This is a default-path leakage risk, though not enough evidence for high severity.
conditions: IF Argo artifacts contain secrets or regulated data
IF Claude Code is pointed at the same workspace or repo containing those artifacts
mitigations: Keep sensitive Argo artifacts outside Claude Code-accessible paths
Redact secrets before writing workflow outputs
Use separate OS users or containers for each agent
Restrict Claude Code to a minimal repo checkout

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo Workflows orchestrates data-engineering artifacts, while Claude Code can write the filesystem, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, and use broad network egress. Both can mutate the same repo or working tree, and Claude Code explicitly shares state via filesystem and git. Without locking, concurrent writes and git-state corruption are a realistic default hazard.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same checkout or git branch
IF Argo emits files that Claude Code edits or commits
mitigations: Assign separate branches or worktrees
Serialize writes with a lock file
Disable automatic git commits by Claude Code
Run Argo and Claude Code in separate directories

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo can produce workflow artifacts and parameters that Claude Code can read and then act on with shell, package-install, and git privileges. If Claude Code treats those outputs as authoritative, a bad workflow result can cascade into destructive edits or commands. The pair therefore has a direct action-taking chain with no built-in verification shown.
conditions: IF Claude Code consumes Argo outputs as task instructions
IF those outputs trigger shell commands, package installs, or git commits
mitigations: Require human approval before shell or git actions
Validate Argo outputs against a schema before use
Mark workflow outputs as untrusted by default
Add a review step before any commit or deployment

E_compliance.rationale: Argo Workflows is an open-source workflow engine with artifacts/parameters, while Claude Code is closed-source, runs as the invoking user, and handles git credentials and API keys. If regulated data or credentials enter shared files, Claude Code's broad egress and local-host execution can create retention or residency mismatches. The evidence is indirect, so I choose medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated data is written into shared files or artifacts
IF Claude Code processes data subject to stricter residency or retention rules than Argo outputs
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Document retention for workflow artifacts and terminal logs
Use separate credentials for each agent
Add deletion procedures for generated files
